title: observability-pipeline-trace-metrics-log-ingestion-debug-notes-wip
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for the ongoing observability pipeline issue (metrics drops + missing traces in downstream storage). Working notes, commands run, output snippets, hypotheses, and next steps. This is a living doc - not polished.

Context / high-level summary:
- Since 2026-02-26 ~03:00 UTC we started seeing a drop in ingest rates for metrics and a concurrent increase in dropped tracing spans reported by the runtime. Logs ingestion seems intermittently delayed but eventually catches up.
- Affects hosted-api and dedicated clusters in us-west-2 primarily.
- Customer impact: delayed dashboards, a few missing traces in flame graphs. No complete outage, but SLO violation risk for 10m latency windows.
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INC-1824 (linked). Slack thread: #obs-prod (see linked_artifacts).

Observed symptoms (raw):
- Metrics aggregated per-minute show a ~40% drop for a subset of metrics from 03:00-04:20 UTC on 2026-02-26.
- Trace-ingest service returned 429s for some upstream producers (rate-limit/overloaded) around same window.
- Router logs show repeated 502 errors when forwarding batched logs to log-ingest pods on one node pool.

Important IDs / examples:
- sample trace_id missing downstream: 6f8a2c7b-4e9e-4d7a-9b2d-2c9f6b3a2a9c
- sample metric key with drop: "service.request.latency.p50" (shard s3)
- affected pod: trace-ingest-5b7c9c6f-ztx2 (node ip: 10.12.45.87)

Commands tried (chronological):
1) Check k8s pod status & restart count:
$ kubectl -n observability get pods -o wide | grep trace-ingest
trace-ingest-5b7c9c6f-ztx2   1/1 Running   3   2d   10.12.45.87   ip-10-12-45-87.us-west-2.compute.internal

2) Tail pod logs for errors around 2026-02-26T03:00UTC:
$ kubectl -n observability logs trace-ingest-5b7c9c6f-ztx2 --since=6h | grep -iE "error|warn|429|502|drop" -n | sed -n '1,200p'
[2026-02-26T02:59:58Z] WARN  incoming-queue size=128 threshold=100 (near capacity)
[2026-02-26T03:01:05Z] ERROR forwarding batch to log-sink: HTTP 502 Bad Gateway (connection reset by peer)
[2026-02-26T03:01:06Z] WARN  rate-limiter: client=service-A blocked (burst exceeded)
[2026-02-26T03:05:12Z] ERROR span write failed: E_WRITE_TIMEOUT (attempt=3)

3) Check node metrics (node exporter) to rule out resource exhaustion:
$ kubectl -n kube-system top node ip-10-12-45-87.us-west-2.compute.internal
CPU(%)   MEMORY(%)
10%      67%
- No OOMs or high CPU. Disk IO nominal.

4) Query TSDB to confirm ingestion delta (clickhouse / metrics-store):
-- ClickHouse-ish pseudo query run via metrics-console
SELECT count() FROM metrics_raw WHERE metric_name = 'service.request.latency.p50' AND timestamp >= '2026-02-26 02:50:00' AND timestamp < '2026-02-26 04:30:00' GROUP BY toStartOfMinute(timestamp) ORDER BY timestamp
-- Result: minute buckets 03:00-03:20 show ~60% fewer rows than baseline.

5) Check trace-router logs for drop counts and rejection reason:
$ kubectl -n observability logs trace-router-846f4d5b -c router --since=12h | grep "dropped" -n | tail -n 50
[2026-02-26T03:01:06Z] INFO  dropped 124 spans: reason=rate-limited target=trace-ingest-5b7c9c6f
[2026-02-26T03:01:07Z] INFO  dropped 98 spans: reason=connection-reset target=log-sink-2

6) Replayed a small sample payload directly to trace-ingest pod via curl to replicate behavior:
$ curl -v -X POST http://10.12.45.87:9411/api/v2/spans -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @sample-trace-batch.json
* Response:
> POST /api/v2/spans HTTP/1.1
> Host: 10.12.45.87:9411
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< {"error":"upstream connection reset"}

7) Inspect service mesh / sidecar for resets (istio-proxy logs):
$ kubectl -n observability logs trace-ingest-5b7c9c6f-ztx2 -c istio-proxy --since=6h | grep "connection reset" -n
[2026-02-26T03:01:05Z] [Envoy] upstream reset: connection failure, host: log-sink.default.svc.cluster.local

8) Check log-sink (downstream) health & restart counts:
$ kubectl -n observability get pods | grep log-sink
log-sink-2-6f9b8c4   1/1 Running   5   5d
$ kubectl -n observability logs log-sink-2-6f9b8c4 --since=6h | grep -i "timeout|error|conn" -n | sed -n '1,200p'
[2026-02-26T03:01:05Z] ERROR write to object store timed out (retry 1)
[2026-02-26T03:02:10Z] WARN  backpressure: queue_size=2048 (threshold=1500)

9) Check ingress throttles / rate-limiter config for trace-router + metrics-collector (ConfigMaps):
$ kubectl -n observability get configmap rate-limits -o yaml | sed -n '1,200p'
# snippet:
trace_router:
  global_rate_per_minute: 120000
  client_burst: 1000
metrics_collector:
  global_rate_per_minute: 200000
  client_burst: 2000

Notes: limits look generous - but rate-limiter still reporting clients blocked, likely due to local burst window.

Error snippets saved:
- "ERROR forwarding batch to log-sink: HTTP 502 Bad Gateway (connection reset by peer)"
- "WARN rate-limiter: client=service-A blocked (burst exceeded)"
- "ERROR span write failed: E_WRITE_TIMEOUT (attempt=3)"
- Envoy: "upstream reset: connection failure, host: log-sink.default.svc.cluster.local"

Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
1) Downstream log-sink (object store writer) had transient IO/latency spike causing connection resets; upstream buffers filled -> rate-limiter tripped -> drops. Evidence: log-sink timeouts + backpressure queue_size high; envoys show upstream reset.
2) One node pool (10.12.45.87) handling disproportionate traffic due to misrouted load balancing or affinity; that pod shows higher restarts/3 restarts vs peers.
3) Recent config change to trace-router or rate-limiter (2026-02-25 22:30 UTC) reduced effective burst window - check GitHub PR and ConfigMap rollout.
4) Network flakiness between trace-ingest node and object-store endpoint (transient packet loss) - less likely given only one node affected.

Quick checks to validate hypotheses (done / TODO):
- DONE: Confirmed log-sink reports timeouts and backpressure.
- DONE: Envoy logs show upstream resets matching same timestamp.
- TODO: Compare traffic distribution across node pools (kube-proxy / service endpoints) to see if shard affinity is wrong.
- TODO: Roll back rate-limiter config to previous snapshot in staging and test with load generator.
- TODO: Reach out to infra-networking to check BGP/ENI/MTU metrics for ip-10-12-45-87 around timestamp.
- TODO: Run targeted kube-proxy / iptables inspect on node to ensure endpoints not stale.

Mitigation attempt (so far):
- Temporarily increased log-sink replica count from 2 -> 4 in us-west-2 to absorb backlog (scaled at 2026-02-26T04:10 UTC). Observed gradual recovery in metrics ingestion by 04:45 UTC.
- Added short-lived override to rate-limiter client_burst for trace-router to 4000 to avoid local blocking while backlog drains (rolled at 2026-02-26T04:15 UTC).

Results after mitigation:
- Metrics ingestion returned to ~95% of baseline by 2026-02-26T05:00 UTC.
- Trace drops reduced but still a few missing spans for the window 03:00-03:20.

Notes / lessons learned:
- Backpressure in log-sink needs clearer SLOs + circuit-breaker behavior upstream to avoid head-of-line blocking for other tenants.
- We should add per-pod health-check metrics for write-latency to object-store (expose to dashboards + alert).

Next steps (action owners):
- Jordan: run endpoint distribution audit across service endpoints + kube-proxy iptables on node ip-10-12-45-87 (by 2026-03-04).
- Maya: open PR to add write-latency metric export from log-sink and a dashboard (JIRA-OPS-1934) (by 2026-03-06).
- Evan: coordinate with infra-networking to check node-level networking around 2026-02-26T03:00 (ticket INFRA-NET-452).
- Sofia: prepare short postmortem draft with timeline and mitigations (by 2026-03-07).

Scratch commands to run next: 
- list endpoints and distribution: $ kubectl -n observability get endpoints trace-ingest -o wide
- dump iptables on node (need privileged access): $ ssh ec2-user@10.12.45.87 sudo iptables-save > /tmp/iptables.dump && scp /tmp/iptables.dump me@workstation
- replay load in staging with same payload rate to measure rate-limiter behavior:
$ ./loadgen --target http://staging-trace-router:9411 --rate 2000/s --duration 5m --payload sample-trace-batch.json

Raw notes / rough thread copies:
- slack #obs-prod (2026-02-26 03:05) @maya: "we see 502s from log-sink, increasing backlog"
- slack #infra (2026-02-26 04:00) @evan: "scaled log-sink to 4, backlog draining"

Appendix: quick grep patterns used frequently:
- find trace id: $ kubectl -n observability logs -l app=trace-ingest --since=24h | grep 6f8a2c7b -n
- search for 502s: $ kubectl -n observability logs --since=12h | grep '502 Bad Gateway' -n

If you read this later: key things to check first = log-sink latency/backpressure + envoy upstream resets + node-specific endpoint distribution. Anything else added here will be consolidated into the postmortem.
